learningObjectives.title: Pre-colonial states, trade and the slave trade
The modern Middle East and post-independence Africa

questions.q: The 'Scramble for Africa' was formalised at the:
questions.explain: European powers set rules for partitioning Africa at the Berlin Conference.

questions.q: Apartheid in South Africa was a system of:
questions.explain: Apartheid (1948-1994) enforced racial segregation and white-minority rule.

questions.q: Nelson Mandela became President of South Africa in:
questions.explain: Mandela was elected in 1994 in South Africa's first fully democratic elections.

questions.q: In 1956 Egypt's President Nasser nationalised the:
questions.explain: Nasser's nationalisation of the Suez Canal triggered the 1956 Suez Crisis.

questions.q: The trans-Atlantic slave trade forcibly transported:
options: Goods along the Silk Road only
questions.explain: Millions of Africans were forcibly transported across the Atlantic to the Americas.

questions.q: Ghana, led by Kwame Nkrumah, became independent in:
questions.explain: Ghana was the first sub-Saharan colony to gain independence, in 1957.

questions.q: Pan-Africanism promoted:
questions.explain: Pan-Africanism encouraged solidarity and independence across Africa.

questions.q: The medieval Mali Empire was renowned for its wealth in:
questions.explain: Mali, under rulers like Mansa Musa, grew rich from gold and Saharan trade.

questions.q: The creation of the state of Israel in 1948 was followed by:
questions.explain: Israel's establishment in 1948 led to conflict with neighbouring Arab states.

questions.q: The Six-Day War (1967) was fought between Israel and:
questions.explain: In 1967 Israel fought Egypt, Jordan and Syria, capturing significant territory.

questions.q: Colonial borders in Africa were problematic because they were often:
options: Drawn by Europeans, cutting across ethnic and cultural groups
questions.explain: Arbitrary colonial borders contributed to later conflicts and instability.

questions.q: The main organisation opposing apartheid in South Africa was the:
questions.explain: The ANC led resistance to apartheid, with Mandela among its leaders.

questions.q: The 1994 Rwandan genocide was directed primarily against the:
questions.explain: Hutu extremists carried out genocide against the Tutsi and moderate Hutu in 1994.

questions.q: Decolonisation across Africa accelerated after:
questions.explain: Weakened European powers and rising nationalism sped up African independence after 1945.

questions.q: The Suez Crisis (1956) involved an intervention against Egypt by:
questions.explain: Britain, France and Israel intervened after Nasser nationalised the Suez Canal.

questions.q: Oil in the modern Middle East has significantly shaped:
questions.explain: Oil wealth became central to Middle Eastern economies and global geopolitics.

questions.q: Apartheid in South Africa ended through:
questions.explain: Negotiations led to the end of apartheid and democratic elections in 1994.

questions.q: The organisation founded in 1963 to promote African cooperation and decolonisation was the:
questions.explain: The OAU (1963) promoted African unity, decolonisation and cooperation.

questions.q: Assessing the causes of African nationalism involves weighing factors such as:
options: Colonial exploitation, the impact of WWII and educated elites
questions.explain: Multiple interacting factors drove the rise of African nationalist movements.

questions.q: Comparing decolonisation in different African states is an example of:
questions.explain: Comparing cases is a central Paper 3 analytical skill.
